page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Oranges and lemons
title: Oranges and lemons
topic: Language for maintaining good customer relations
description:
Tense times at Tip Top Trading! Anna is having trouble working with new employee Rachel, who's making some big mistakes. What can Anna do before Rachel goes too far? How can she salvage the company's good customer relations?
This episode focuses on what to say when you have to maintain good relations with your customers.
phrases: Hello I'm Anna from Tip Top Trading. How are you today?
I hope you have received our order and are happy with it.
We do hope you are pleased with our service and that you may use us again.
Do you have any questions you may want to ask?

listening_challenge.question: What item have both Denise and Tom lost?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello and welcome again to English at Work, where things are a little tense. Anna is finding it hard to work with new employee, Rachel. She's told Paul, the boss, about Rachel's incompetence but he’s done nothing about it.
So Anna, how are you feeling today?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Frustrated. All that work I put in, getting the contract for Imperial Lemons and Rachel has sent out a load of second-hand plastic oranges!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: I guess you're going to have to call your client and sort out the mess.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I guess so. Oh hi Tom.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Is she about? The man-eater?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No it's all clear, she's gone out for a cappuccino.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Good good. Look I managed to call the guy she bought the second-hand oranges from, and I cancelled the order.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Phew, great!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah… and last night I managed to order some Imperial Lemons and sent them to that company in France – Fruit Traders International. Here’s the paperwork.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom, that's brilliant! Here, let me give you a big hug – you saved the day!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ooh, that's a bit tight.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh not again! You two just can't leave each other alone…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Bbbut it was just…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Say no more Anna. Now, I was looking for my special red pen, have you seen it anywhere?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No. Funny that, my pens have gone missing too.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I'll go and get some more.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Now Anna, I don't want to interfere but have you called that company in France to see how they are?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, they're fine aren’t they?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: It's good customer service to call them and see how they are.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But what do I say?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Tell you what. I'll go over there and you can call me and practise.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right. OK Tom, I'm calling your number now.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hello – Fruit Traders International.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, hello…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: …introduce yourself and ask me how I am.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. Hello I'm Anna from Tip Top Trading. How are you today?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I'm very well. Now ask me about the order.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I hope you have received our Imperial Lemons and that you are happy with the order.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes, very very happy. The lemons are… fantastique!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh that's good. Erm… we do hope you are pleased with our service and that you may use us again.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: We certainly will. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Do you have any questions you may want to ask?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No… actually yes…. err, can I… err… buy you dinner sometime?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Very funny Tom. They won't ask that!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No. I'm asking you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right… erm… OK then… yes!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hooray! Or should I say oh dear? Silly Anna has agreed to go on a dinner date with Tom – but there is still some business to attend to. Don't forget to make that call to your client Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No I won't – in fact I'll do it right now.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Good! While she makes that call, here is a reminder of some of the phrases she could use…

transcript.speaker: Hello I'm Anna from Tip Top Trading. How are you today?
transcript.text:
I hope you have received our order and are happy with it.
We do hope you are pleased with our service and that you may use us again.
Do you have any questions you may want to ask?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Are you OK Anna? You look a bit annoyed.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I am – I just called our client in France to check everything was OK and they said Rachel had already called them and told them our lemons were so last season and they would be stupid not to choose oranges!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That's terrible.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: …hey Anna, how about this restaurant for our date… I mean our business meeting. Look at this menu…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Not now Tom. Rachel has messed things up again. She's causing so much trouble. She's got to go.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh… yeah right. This calls for action.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: It certainly does. It sounds like Rachel has gone too far this time and it's up to Anna to sort things out. But what can she do? Join us again next time on English at Work to find out. Bye!
